newsitem.title: ITALY: Lawyers in leniency plea for Venice tower raiders.
newsitem.headline: Lawyers in leniency plea for Venice tower raiders.

text.p: Lawyers defending eight separatists on trial for storming the belltower in Venice's St Mark's Square two months ago appealed on Tuesday to the court to show leniency.
Franco Antonelli, a lawyer for one of the defendants, said none of the separatists had inflicted harm on anybody in their bizarre assault on the belltower.

State prosecutor Rita Ugolini last week called for five of the men to be sentenced to nine years and the remaining three to be jailed for eight years and two months. Almost all of the men are in their 20s and 30s.
The Assize Court is expected to hand down a sentence on Wednesday after all pleas from the defence have been heard.
"The prosecutor has asked for a frightful sentence for these boys," said Antonelli. "A sentence of eight or nine years would mean that their lives would be finished."
Fausto Faccia, another defending lawyer, said the defendents should serve no more than two years, which under Italian law would allow the sentence to be suspended.
The eight broke into the belltower during the night after hijacking a ferry to take them and a home-made armoured car to the square in the lagoon city.

Calling themselves soldiers of the "Most serene Republic" of Venice, a centuries-old maritime power before its fall 200 years ago, the eight unfurled a flag of the republic and shouted separatist slogans.
They were charged with kidnapping the ferry captain, subversion, illegal weapons possession, threatening public officials and occupying church property.
Maverick Italian poltician Marco Pannella told reporters at the trial that he hoped the court would be even-handed in its sentencing.
"These are things I could have done myself," said Pannella, a civil rights activist who rose to prominence in the mid-1970s when he campaigned successfully for the legalisation of divorce.
